entries.author: Maxim
entries.subject: Do not call a queued message unread when a worker finishes
entries.decision: Port the reporting fix through ChatBBC's current run-scoped worker inbox. Never-offered rows for a reusable sleeping worker are described as still queued; exact prime-family/run/conversation ownership remains unchanged.

entries.author: Maxim
entries.subject: Repair project page titles and answer /hello honestly without a protocol
entries.decision: Port protocol-less /hello as identification-only tri-state compatibility while keeping all privileged routes protocol-strict; reject project shell titles at the existing session-title owner without changing conversation or manual-title authority.

entries.author: Maxim
entries.subject: Remove invisible characters from stored API keys
entries.decision: Normalize invisible paste characters at ChatBBC's encrypted credential owner for API-key slots only. Existing secure-storage availability, mutation queue, cache publication and non-API secret semantics remain authoritative.

entries.author: Maxim
entries.subject: Show replies that point to other content instead of the raw pointer
entries.decision: Port provider content-reference presentation through one shared resolver. A recorded same-message native rendering may resolve presentation, but it never creates conversation, turn, request, or session authority.

entries.subject: Merge pull request #576 from Maximapple/fix/content-reference-directive

entries.subject: Handle any unknown ChatGPT directive instead of one fix per name

changes.decision: Hosted GitHub Actions workflows are not imported. Build, test and release run on the local Linux x64 host, so the three workflow files are deleted rather than translated. Upstream Intel-macOS retry and standalone-extension ZIP workflow changes therefore have no downstream execution owner.
changes.portRule: Translate only platform-independent upstream workflow intent that applies to the Linux x64 local release into a local script under scripts/ and map it. Never restore a file under .github/workflows, Intel/macOS runner policy, or a standalone companion ZIP release path.

changes.decision: The package, app, bridge, extension and connector identity is ChatBBC: slug chatbbc, protocol 18, app ID com.chatbbc.app, and the three connectors ChatBBC Core, Desktop and Plugins. ChatBBC's downstream version is independently 2.2.0; upstream 2.1.19/2.1.20 version-only bumps are provenance, not downstream release authority. Live product strings are renamed; tool schemas, route shapes and pairing behavior are unchanged.
changes.portRule: Reapply the ChatBBC identity values and independent downstream version policy on every port. The slug and the protocol are independent fail-closed gates, so bump or rename them separately and update both sides together. Never inherit an upstream release version merely because functional commits are ported.

changes.decision: Extension and renderer locale catalogs name ChatBBC in every live product string, with descriptive prose translated per locale. The catalog artwork copyright attribution is preserved in each renderer locale.
changes.portRule: Translate new product strings into every locale file and keep ChatBBC itself untranslated. Preserve the catalog artwork copyright sentence; do not machine-translate authored or provider text.

changes.decision: Provider directives are interpreted by one shared resolver. ChatBBC keeps its writing-block renderer, identity fences and sanitized message renderer while adopting upstream content-reference behavior.
changes.portRule: Port provider directive syntax/resolution through src/shared/content-reference.ts. Captured HTML is same-message presentation evidence only; never use it to infer conversation, turn, request or session ownership. Preserve ChatBBC writing blocks and sanitizer behavior.
checks: npx vitest run test/content-reference.test.ts test/renderer-html.test.ts test/goal.test.ts test/session.test.ts

changes.decision: The upstream composer refinement is ported as presentation over ChatBBC's existing draft, Goal, outbox and model-observation owners. Composer motion never owns resting geometry; context values remain local estimates. The same files also preserve ChatBBC content-reference rendering, public identity and live Omarchy palette behavior.
changes.portRule: Port composer layout, motion, mode/model controls and verification without introducing a second send, draft, Goal, model or theme owner. Preserve ChatBBC identity strings, shared provider-directive handling and Omarchy variables whenever upstream changes chat.ts, index.html or styles.css.
checks: npx vitest run test/composer-motion.test.ts test/context-meter.test.ts test/renderer-layout.test.ts

changes.decision: ChatBBC adopts the opt-in read-only local control API as a projection of existing connection, bridge, plugin, update and call-context owners. The listener owns no application state, defaults off, binds loopback only, and publishes only an explicit non-secret status schema. Renderer/preload settings expose only the enablement boolean and use the existing stale-safe three-way settings merge.
changes.portRule: Keep the control API disabled by default and fail malformed config to off. Preserve serialized start/stop/shutdown, per-process token files, Origin/Host/auth/body/rate fences and allowlist-only status projection. Settings may start or stop it only when the authoritative config switch actually changes; never expose endpoint/token secrets to renderer state or turn this into another MCP surface, browser bridge, session owner or settings authority.
checks: npx vitest run test/config.test.ts test/control-api.test.ts test/ipc.test.ts

changes.decision: Product names in the coding, session and handoff prompts and in the plugin catalog explanation are ChatBBC. Capability contracts, tool authority, limits and the catalog artwork copyright comment are unchanged.
changes.portRule: Reapply the ChatBBC naming when merging prompt fixes. Do not alter tool authority, validation, limits or provider-policy statements, and keep the catalog artwork copyright line.

changes.decision: One original speech-bubble lettermark in artwork/chatbbc-mark.svg is the single source; the icon generator rasterizes it into the app, tray and extension icons. The companion popup and overlay use neutral grayscale styling.
changes.portRule: Regenerate icon outputs from artwork/chatbbc-mark.svg rather than editing them by hand. Keep the companion styling neutral and do not inject rules into ChatGPT's own transcript.

changes.decision: The desktop follows the live Omarchy palette through one main-process reader. The palette is projected over saved Appearance settings while Follow Omarchy theme is on and is never written back into config.
changes.portRule: Keep the live palette in the main-process owner and out of persisted config. Merge functional fixes into the shared appearance owner; do not add a second snapshot, poller or theme-sync protocol.

changes.decision: The only supported distribution is a Linux x64 AppImage named ChatBBC-Linux-x64.AppImage, built and verified on the local host. Windows, macOS and ARM release targets, aliases and builder configuration are removed. Official Sharp WebAssembly replaces the native Linux payload because the Electron/GLib combination crashes during image processing; license and source inventory track the shipped module. The local release script builds a checked candidate and publishes only on explicit invocation.
changes.portRule: Keep the release target Linux x64 AppImage with a packaged-runtime image decode probe and an exact source/license inventory for its WebAssembly payload. Bind explicit publication's Git remote and gh operations to the same preflighted repository; bound packaged-smoke child shutdown. Translate new upstream packaging checks into local scripts; never restore hosted workflows or a Windows, macOS or ARM release target.

changes.decision: Local verification and fetch scripts name ChatBBC in their fixtures, window titles and User-Agent strings, and scripts/verify-local-ui.mjs runs the Wayland GUI fixtures on the local host instead of a hosted runner. Platform-specific Intel-macOS retry configuration is not adopted into the Linux-local Vitest policy.
changes.portRule: Keep verification local and on Wayland/Linux x64. Rename product strings in fixtures when the identity changes, and do not point a fixture at a hosted runner or a predecessor product name. Do not import retry policy whose only owner is an unsupported upstream release platform.

changes.decision: Current docs, the agent guide and issue templates name ChatBBC, target Linux x64 and point at local commands. Upstream provenance links and historical reports stay, while upstream 2.1.19/2.1.20 release notes, upstream composer worklog material and upstream changelog release claims are not copied into current ChatBBC documentation. Hosted-CI badges and Windows, macOS and ARM download promises are gone.
changes.portRule: Reapply the ChatBBC naming and Linux x64 scope to current docs. Keep upstream provenance links and genuinely historical reports as historical; map target-baseline-only upstream release notes/worklogs as intentional downstream omissions after the target baseline becomes authoritative. Never present an upstream release/changelog entry as a ChatBBC release, restore a hosted-CI badge, or add a non-Linux download promise.

changes.decision: Test fixtures and assertions use the ChatBBC identity, protocol 18 and the three ChatBBC connector names. Tests that pin a predecessor name do so to prove it is rejected.
changes.portRule: Update fixtures to the ChatBBC identity when a port changes observable identity. Keep a predecessor literal only in a test that proves it is rejected, and record that literal under retainedIdentifiers.

changes.decision: Two local guards replace the hosted workflow checks: verify-upstream-map accounts for every added, modified and deleted path exactly once, and verify-rebrand accounts for every predecessor product literal.
changes.portRule: Extend the guards when a port adds an identity surface or a map field, and map the guards themselves. Do not weaken either check to make a port pass.

changes.decision: docs/upstream-map.json is the machine-readable authority for which downstream path belongs to which decision; docs/UPSTREAM.md is the porting runbook; the committed superpowers spec and plan are downstream migration records and remain ChatBBC-owned documentation.
changes.portRule: Update the map in the same change as the port. Advance the pinned upstream commit only after the whole upstream delta is accounted for; record a partial port in ports instead. Keep the migration spec/plan as downstream records rather than attempting to source them from upstream.
